How few polygons can fourteen points make?
Imagine stretching a rubber band around a selection of points.
Count it if every selected point touches the band at a corner.
Each triangle counts, but a point tucked inside disqualifies that selection.
For ten and eleven points, Nikol Savova found the minima: 189 and 283.
With twelve points, the minimum rises to 408.
This arrangement reaches it with 220 triangles, 165 quadrilaterals, 22 pentagons and one hexagon.
With thirteen points, the minimum is 570.
Exactly five arrangements attain it, up to order type: what matters is which way each triple turns.
With fourteen points, the minimum is 780. Just one order type attains it.
It gives 364 triangles, 350 quadrilaterals, 64 pentagons, and two hexagons.
The proof tests possible turn patterns and rules out impossible ones using triangle areas.
These are exact answers for small sets. How the minimum grows in general remains open.
